timestamps.note: timestamps equal frame_index/fps: loop timing is not recorded, the jitter check in data.py cannot fire

units.reason: legacy LeRobot degrees (tick = 180/2048 deg verified on every arm joint)

blas.config: OpenBLAS 0.3.34.106.0  USE64BITINT DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY SkylakeX MAX_THREADS=64

conventions.recording: Legacy LeRobot (ManipulatorRobot.teleop_step, `main_*` names): the goal a[t] is WRITTEN to the follower first and the follower state x[t] is READ afterwards (a few ms later), so x[t] may already contain a few ms of response to a[t] (act-then-observe).
conventions.replay: Replay (identical for both conventions): q_sim[0]=x[0] (zero velocity); for t=0..T-2 apply ctrl=a[t-d] (d = fitted integer command delay, stock d=0) for the whole frame, step `substeps` physics steps (timestep set so substeps*timestep = 1/fps exactly), record q_sim[t+1]; sim and real are compared at the same index t=1..T-1. The real sub-frame send-to-read offset (legacy: a[t] sent a few ms BEFORE x[t] is read; current: a[t] sent a few ms AFTER) is not modelled; it is absorbed by the fitted dynamics/delay, and it shifts lags between the two conventions by a fraction of a frame in opposite directions.
conventions.lag: lag = argmin_L Var(a[t] - y[t+L]) over a fixed window t in [0, T-10), parabolic sub-frame refinement; y = real or sim state. Includes the 1-frame sampling offset: in the replay and in observe-then-act (current LeRobot) recordings an instantaneous actuator measures 1.0 frame; in act-then-observe (legacy) recordings it would measure ~0, and a realistic servo measures its delay minus the few-ms write-to-read gap. Lags are therefore directly comparable between sim and real within one dataset, and only approximately (fraction of a frame) across codebases. Also reported in ms, since datasets differ in fps. Joints with command std < 1 deg in an episode are skipped.
conventions.angles: physical degrees (encoder ticks * 360/4096), arm joints only
conventions.change: relative change of an error metric, new/reference - 1; NEGATIVE = better

split.method: future = last round(n*test_frac) episodes by index; interleaved = round(n*test_frac) episodes of the rest drawn by numpy default_rng(seed).permutation, plus every remaining episode beyond the fit cap; fit = the remaining episodes (<= max_train_episodes)

mapping.note: legacy LeRobot zero pose = arm straight horizontal (feetech_calibration.py); the MJCF zero (from the SO-ARM100 URDF) is also the arm stretched horizontally forward, so nominal offsets are 0. Documented signs +1 (MJCF joint axes); legacy LeRobot sets each motor's direction from the user's 'rotated position', so signs are checked per dataset against the recorded range of motion (mapping_checks).

baseline.model: y[t+1] = y[t] + alpha*(a[t-d] + b - y[t]), y[0] = x[0], per arm joint

limitations: Open-loop joint-space replay only: contacts are disabled in simulation, objects/table are not modelled; episodes where the real arm pushes on the world show up as sim-vs-real error that no actuator calibration can remove.
Gripper excluded from all metrics (object contact); it is driven by a linear map of its 0-100 range onto the MJCF jaw range.

The servo is modelled as MuJoCo's ideal PD position actuator with a torque limit (stock forcerange); the real STS3215 firmware (P-only position loop, acceleration profile, deadband) is approximated, not reproduced. The fitted kp is therefore a bandwidth parameter of that model, not the servo's static stiffness (compare the gravity-sag audit).

Fitted per joint: kp, kv, frictionloss; shared: integer command delay. Armature is fixed at the stock value (only the bandwidth kp/I_eff is identifiable from position trajectories); the identifiable combinations (natural frequency, damping ratio) are reported with CIs.

Zero offsets are NOT fitted: the twin uses the documented calibration convention (sign checked per joint). In v1 fitted offsets were unidentified, went to their +-20 deg bounds and degraded forward-kinematic plausibility. A robot whose calibration zero differs from the convention is therefore modelled with a wrong gravity load.

Joint limits: a stock MJCF limit that the fit episodes cross by > 0.5 deg is released (no stop); others stay at stock. Held-out motion past a non-released stock limit is clipped by the twin (fraction reported).
Command delay is an integer number of frames shared by all joints.
Dataset timestamps are nominal (frame_index/fps); real control-loop timing, jitter and overruns are unobservable and unmodelled.
One dataset = one physical robot and setup: the calibrated twin is a model of that robot, not of the robot type; transfer to other units is not tested here.

Confidence intervals are percentile bootstraps over episodes (whole episodes resampled, 10,000 draws, fixed seed); with 12 future / 12 interleaved held-out episodes they are approximate and tend to be slightly too narrow. They do not cover the choice of split, of fit configuration, or of dataset.
Recorded with legacy LeRobot (act-then-observe); lags are not exactly comparable with current-LeRobot (observe-then-act) datasets (see conventions).

Stock MJCF limits crossed by the fit episodes and released in the aligned/calibrated twins: shoulder_lift lower, wrist_flex upper. The stock twin is held at those limits (counted as stock-twin error).
future held-out episodes leave the fit episodes' range of motion (+-2 deg) on more than 5% of frames: {'wrist_roll': 0.1157}.
Fitted parameters at a bound (within BOUND_TOL): frictionloss[shoulder_lift]; the value is a bound, not an estimate.

Not identified individually (marginal/conditional std ratio >= 10): kp[shoulder_pan]. Only combinations of them are constrained by the data (see identifiability); individual values are not meaningful.
interleaved: final-pose (static) gap is larger for the calibrated twin than for stock on shoulder_lift, elbow_flex by point estimate; CIs separate on shoulder_lift, elbow_flex.
